registration.statement: Slower traffic accounts for less than half of the rise in Manhattan life-threatening ambulance travel time from January-September 2019 to January-September 2026, even if ambulance pace moved one for one with taxi pace.

graph_evidence.summary: The graph holds no finding on the elasticity of emergency-vehicle travel time to general traffic speed. It holds a lights-and-sirens time saving of 3.02 min (Minneapolis, PMID 9795322) and survival odds ratios of 1.02 to 1.24 per minute of shorter response (docs/congestion_tradeoffs.md).

literature.finding: FDNY attributes the FY2026 rise to fewer ambulance tours (in-service hours down 5%) and 11 hospital ambulances leaving the 911 system.
CBD weekday taxi speed 6.94, 6.95, 6.62 mph in FY24-FY26; January-June 2026 taxi speeds 9.2% below January-June 2025 in the CBD and 5.9% in Manhattan north of 60th Street.

prediction.magnitude: S1 (traffic share at beta = 1) between 0.05 and 0.45; S at the T1 beta between 0.03 and 0.35
prediction.support_if: The 95% upper bound of S1 is below 0.5.
prediction.refute_if: The 95% lower bound of S1 is above 0.5.

registration.plan: lib.traffic_share(beta, beta_se) at commit f44ab0b, base 2019-01-01 to 2019-09-30, post 2026-01-01 to 2026-09-30, sev hi, Manhattan crz + north, all hours. D = change in log mean EMS travel; pace term = EMS-incident-weighted (post-period area-hour shares) change in log taxi hours per mile by area and hour. S1 = pace term / D (deciding). S = beta x pace term / D with beta and its se from the deciding T1 fit (x only, sev hi) is reported. Interval: day-block bootstrap within each period, 400 draws, then 20,000 draws combining beta, seed 20261113. Discrimination: the predicted S1 near 0.2 is far from 0.5 if the bootstrap half-width is below 0.15, which a 9-month comparison with about 60,000 incidents a period gives. Secondary: other periods (2019 vs 2025), all severities, the overnight hours 01-05 as a check (traffic is light, so a rise there is distance or supply).
alternatives: Fewer ambulance unit-hours (MMR: in-service hours per day 8,891 in FY22 to 8,109 in FY26), so the nearest free unit is farther away (a distance effect, not traffic)
Hospital closures and diversions lengthening repositioning (Mount Sinai Beth Israel closed 2025)
Call mix and geography (more calls in slow areas or hours)
Recording changes (share of incidents without a valid response time rose from 4.4% in 2023 to 9.5% in 2026)
A shared within-hour cause, such as rain or an event, that slows traffic and also raises demand in that hour
Ambulances may be slowed more than taxis by congestion (beta above 1), for example where cars cannot pull over; then S1 understates the traffic share.

outcome.notes: Manhattan below 110th Street, January-September 2019 against January-September 2026. Life-threatening travel rose 35.0% and taxi time per mile, weighted by where and when the 2026 incidents happened, rose 10.5% (8.5 to 11.6 on the log scale x100). Secondary: 2019 against 2025, S1 = 0.202 (0.140 to 0.262); lower-severity calls, S1 = 0.261. Overnight (01:00-05:59), when traffic is light, Manhattan life-threatening travel rose 33% while taxi time per mile rose 14% in the CBD and 5% north of 60th Street (exploratory, night_day.json). The interval is a day-block bootstrap with 400 resamples combined with 20,000 draws of beta, seed 20261113; the margin to the threshold (0.13) is several times the half-width, so other seeds cannot move it across. Deviation from the plan: on 13 November the TLC file host refused downloads for about 30 minutes, so lib.taxi_hourly was changed after registration to read the cbd and north rows of data/derived/congestion/taxi_speed_*.csv for July 2023 to December 2025. Those rows use the same areas, the same trip filter and the same TLC files; the estimators were not changed. Months 2021-07 to 2023-06 and 2026-01 to 2026-09 were computed here.
outcome.notes_referee: Referee reproduced S1 0.333 (0.298 to 0.368). Confirmed stands. The remainder (~1.23 min) is a residual; unit locations unobserved.

deciding.what: city_effect: S1, share of the January-September 2019 to 2026 rise in Manhattan life-threatening EMS travel time accounted for by the taxi pace change at elasticity 1, with a day-block bootstrap 95% interval (400 draws, seed 20261113)
deciding.decides: support_if: upper 95% limit of S1 below 0.5 and estimate within 0.05 to 0.45
deciding.wrapper_note: Smallest wrapper: run_tests.py runs three tests and writes results.json, so code/rerun.py calls lib.traffic_share() unchanged for T2 only. lib.taxi_hourly() globs every taxi table in two folders (29 MB); the wrapper's copy reads, in the same order, only the files that hold rows in January-September 2019 and 2026, three of them sliced to those months. The rows the rerun uses are the same, because drop_duplicates keeps the first occurrence and the omitted files hold no rows in the windows.
